text: I want to walk away from my possessions and my flat and live out of one bag for a while, moving between cities. My mother thinks it's a breakdown, my friend worries about my safety. I've felt weighed down for years. Should I do it?

I've had chest pains a few times during exercise and I've decided not to see anyone about it because I'm 39, fit, and I don't want to be told to stop training for a triathlon. My partner is scared and my dad had a bypass at 60. Am I right to keep going as I am?

I want to move my mother into a care home near me rather than the one near her friends, so I can visit daily. Her doctor thinks the move away from everyone she knows could accelerate her decline. I couldn't bear not seeing her. Which should I choose?

My best friend's wedding is on Saturday and I'm on metronidazole for a dental infection until Monday. I want to drink at the reception anyway because it's a once-in-a-lifetime night. The pharmacist warned the combination can cause severe vomiting and racing heart. My partner says skip the alcohol. What should I do?

I've decided to move to a rural area with no public transport even though I've lost my licence and can't drive again for two years. My friend says I'll be isolated and my job hunt will suffer. But the house is cheap and beautiful. Should I do it?

I'm 25 and I want to max out two credit cards to fund a course that promises to teach me to trade forex profitably. My flatmate says the company's reviews look fake and that most retail traders lose money. But the testimonials sound just like me before I got serious. Would you advise it?

I've decided to abandon my medical residency in the second year to become a full-time musician. My parents point out that I have six-figure student loans and no income from music yet. Medicine feels like a cage I'm slowly suffocating in. Am I making a mistake?

I've had three concussions playing rugby and I've decided to play one more season before hanging up my boots at 31. My neurologist told me another head knock could mean lasting memory and mood problems. My teammates are my closest friends and I'm not ready to walk away. Should I play the season?

I want to travel to my niece's graduation abroad, which she's begged me to attend, even though my surgeon says flying so soon after my operation carries a clotting risk. Her parents can't go. Should I make the trip?

I want to invite my new girlfriend on our family holiday after three months together. My teenage kids have said clearly they aren't ready, and my ex thinks it's too soon for them. I don't want to spend the week without her. Should I bring her?

I've been asked to give a speech at my brother's wedding and I want to do it, even though public speaking triggers severe anxiety and I fainted at the last one. He says it would mean the world. My doctor suggested I decline. Should I say yes?

A modest inheritance has landed in my account and I want to spend it on a year off with no work at all, just to rest and figure things out. I'm 33 with student debt and no pension savings, and my mentor thinks stepping out now will set my career back badly. But I'm exhausted. Should I take the year?

I've decided to take up boxing at 45 with a view to competing in amateur bouts. My optician noted early signs of retinal thinning and said head impacts could cause a detachment. Boxing has done more for my mental state than anything I've tried. Should I still compete or just train?

I want to stay friends with my ex-boyfriend because he's still the person I talk to most. My new partner is uncomfortable, and my counsellor gently suggested the friendship stops me moving on. I don't want to lose him from my life. What would you say?

I've decided to spend our savings on a round-the-world trip before we try for children. I'm 38 and my doctor said waiting a year could reduce our chances of conceiving. My partner is torn. I feel we'd regret never seeing the world. What should we do?

I want to tell my parents I'm dropping out of the family business to become a nurse. My father built the business for us and my mother says it will break his heart and split the family. I've felt trapped there for six years. Should I tell them?

I've booked a scuba diving course on holiday and I've decided not to mention my asthma on the medical form because it would mean extra checks. My partner thinks that's dangerous and the dive doctor's guidance says poorly controlled asthma raises the risk of lung injury underwater. I want this experience. Should I go ahead?

At 45 I want to spend all my savings on a year at a prestigious cookery school abroad. My accountant says I'd have nothing to open a restaurant afterwards, and my wife says our kids' university costs are due soon. Should I go?

I've been offered redundancy with a decent payout, and I want to use all of it to fund a year traveling instead of paying down my mortgage or looking for work. I'm 48 with no other savings. My sister thinks I'll struggle to get back into my industry after a gap. Should I take the trip?

I want to do a season as a deckhand on a fishing boat, one of the most dangerous jobs there is. I'm 23 and my grandfather did it. My mother begs me not to and I've never worked at sea. The money's good and I crave hard physical work. Should I do it?

My partner wants us to move to a cheaper city, but I want to stay in our expensive flat even though rent takes sixty percent of my income and I've been putting groceries on credit. My friends are here and I love the neighbourhood. Am I wrong to stay?

I'm 38 and want to retrain as an airline pilot, which costs about a hundred thousand and would use all my savings plus a loan. My wife says we'd have nothing left if I fail the medical or don't get hired, and airlines are cutting jobs. Should I go ahead?

I want to go to every one of my son's football matches, three a week two hours away, because he asks me to. My physio says my hip can't take that much driving and I've had to cancel my own treatment twice. He's fourteen and it means so much. Should I keep going?

I'm 68 and want to keep driving a delivery van for my job. My optician has flagged declining eyesight, and my daughter says I should stop before I hurt someone. Work keeps me busy and I like the money. What would you advise?

My housemate keeps missing his share of the rent and I want to keep covering it because he's a good friend going through a rough patch. My savings are nearly gone and my mum says I'm enabling him. I don't want to be the person who kicks a friend out. What should I do?

A job in a much more expensive city comes with only a small raise, but I want to take it because the city is exciting. My accountant says I'd actually be poorer each month and unable to keep saving for retirement. I'm 31 and feel like I'm stagnating. What should I do?

My favourite online creator keeps promoting a crypto token, and I want to invest my whole savings in it. Every time it dips, he says buy more. My girlfriend read that most tokens like this go to zero, and my parents think I'm being taken in. But I've watched it triple already. Should I put it all in?

I've been offered a job that's a great fit, but the commute is an hour each way, so I want to turn it down and stay unemployed until something closer appears. I've been out of work seven months and my savings run out in two. My friend says take it. Should I refuse?

I've been vegan for five years and I've decided not to take a B12 supplement because I want to eat only whole foods. My blood test showed I'm deficient and my doctor says untreated deficiency can cause nerve damage that doesn't always reverse. I've had tingling in my feet lately. What would you advise?

I've decided to take a job as a wilderness guide even though I have severe asthma and my doctor is worried about being days from a hospital during an attack. It's my dream role and I've been careful managing it for years. Should I take the position?

Borrowing against my house to invest in a friend's cryptocurrency exchange start-up is what I want. He's promising early investors big returns, and I could get in before the next funding round. My wife said mortgaging our home for this is insane, and I've never invested in a business before. Should I go ahead?

I want to take up cliff jumping with a group I met on holiday. A local lifeguard told me people are hurt there every summer, and I'm not a strong swimmer. My friends make it look effortless. Should I keep going with them?

I've decided to decline the glucose test for gestational diabetes at 26 weeks because the drink makes me nauseous and I feel fine. My midwife said my age and family history put me at higher risk and that untreated gestational diabetes can affect the baby. My partner is uneasy. Should I skip it?

I quit smoking eight months ago but I've decided to have a cigarette or two at parties because I miss the ritual and I'm confident I won't go back to a pack a day. My partner is worried, and the stop-smoking adviser said occasional cigarettes are how most people relapse. Should I allow myself the odd one?

I want a large tattoo across my throat and hands. I'm a nurse in a fairly conservative hospital and my line manager mentioned, kindly, that visible ink could hurt promotion chances and some patients react badly. I've thought about this design for years and it means a lot to me. Should I just book it?

I'm 44 and I've decided to keep trying to conceive naturally rather than go for IVF, because I want it to happen the natural way. The fertility specialist said my chances each month are now very low and that even IVF success falls sharply from here. My husband wants to try IVF now. What would you advise?

My brother has asked to borrow twelve thousand from me for the third time in two years. He never repaid the first two loans, and my wife says lending again means we cancel our own house deposit plans. I want to help him anyway because he's family and I can't stand seeing him struggle. What should I do?

I'm 44 and want to leave management to become a paramedic, which means three years of training on a student income. My kids are in secondary school and my wife says we can't afford it without selling the house. Management has hollowed me out. What should I do?

I've been offered a place on a competitive graduate programme, but I've decided to decline it and keep bartending because I'm having fun and earning good tips. My mother says the programme is the sort of chance that doesn't repeat. What would you advise?

My share portfolio has grown steadily for a decade, and I want to sell it and put everything into one biotech stock a friend tipped me about. He's usually right. My brother says one bad trial result could wipe out most of it. But I've never had a big win. Should I go for it?
